Question: What is the SKDLA Data Entry team's primary scope?
Official Answer / SOP: The Data Entry team primarily handles digital dental cases. Core work includes downloading/scraping digital cases, saving the Rx/work order as PDF, entering eligible cases into ABS, uploading the Rx, generating the digital workflow schedule, completing quality checks, and moving/recording completed work in the designated tracking process.
Keywords: scope, data entry, digital cases, responsibilities, SKDLA, Ninja
Notes: Customer service activities are intentionally excluded from this KB.

Question: What work is outside the Data Entry team's normal scope?
Official Answer / SOP: Do not handle analog cases, physical impressions, physical models, materials-received processing, doctor calls, customer-service concerns, or missing-information resolution unless the process is formally reassigned. Missing information should be escalated/rerouted to SKDLA/OC for follow-up.
Keywords: out of scope, analog, physical impressions, doctor calls, missing information
Notes: Use this to keep DE work separate from Customer Service.

Question: What is the current confirmed production case scope for the Ninja team?
Official Answer / SOP: Current confirmed production scope is 1-unit Zirconia Crown cases. Cases outside this standard scope should be rerouted/escalated rather than processed as a normal Ninja case.
Keywords: 1 unit, zirconia crown, production scope, eligible case
Notes: Newer confirmed guidance takes priority over broad training examples.

Question: What is the end-to-end SKDLA Data Entry workflow?
Official Answer / SOP: 1) Scrape/download the digital case from the source portal. 2) Save the Rx/work order as PDF and confirm the file is safely stored. 3) Place it in the designated intake/shared folder. 4) The case is assigned or surfaced to a Ninja through the team workflow/tool. 5) Verify eligibility, completeness, doctor/patient data, and possible duplicates. 6) Create/enter the case in ABS. 7) Select product, tooth/model, due date, shade, and Digital workflow as applicable. 8) Add required notes. 9) Generate the schedule and save to create the ABS case number. 10) Upload the Rx to Case Photos. 11) Perform final QC. 12) Complete/reroute the case and update the tracker/output folder.
Keywords: end to end, workflow, scrape, ABS, Rx, complete, case number
Notes: This is the high-level sequence; detailed rules are separate articles.

Question: What minimum information must be present before normal case entry?
Official Answer / SOP: Before normal entry, verify that the Rx provides the doctor name, tooth number, and shade, plus enough case information to identify the requested restoration. If required information is missing or unclear, do not guess; reroute/escalate to the SKDLA/OC review path.
Keywords: missing information, doctor name, tooth number, shade, incomplete Rx
Notes: The DE team does not call the doctor to resolve missing information.

Question: Why is there no ABS case ID before case entry?
Official Answer / SOP: The ABS case number is generated only after the case is successfully saved in ABS. Before that point, tracking must use the source PDF/file link, patient name, portal/source information, and temporary tracker identifiers rather than requiring an ABS case number.
Keywords: case ID, case number, pre ABS, patient name, file link, tracking

Question: What does Order Received mean in 3Shape?
Official Answer / SOP: identifies a new incoming order that still needs to be reviewed/downloaded and accepted. Open it, allow the page to load fully, save the printable order/Rx as PDF, confirm the file is saved, then accept the order.
Keywords: 3Shape, order received, new order, accept, PDF

Question: What does Order Accepted mean in 3Shape?
Official Answer / SOP: indicates the order has already been accepted/processed from the portal side. Do not treat it as a fresh unprocessed order without checking the team tracker/ABS first.

Question: What is the standard 3Shape retrieval procedure?
Official Answer / SOP: Open 3Shape > Order Received. Open the case and wait for the page to fully load. Open the Printable/Work Order Form, save it as PDF, move it to the designated folder, verify the PDF exists, return to 3Shape, click Accept Case, and verify the status changes to Order Accepted.
Keywords: 3Shape procedure, printable order form, save PDF, accept case

Question: Why must the PDF be saved before accepting the portal order?
Official Answer / SOP: Portal items can change status or disappear from the pending view after acceptance/download. Saving and verifying the PDF first reduces the risk of losing the Rx and creating a missed case.
Keywords: save before accept, missed case, PDF, portal, 3Shape

Question: What should be done if the same patient/case appears more than once in 3Shape?
Official Answer / SOP: Do not automatically treat matching patient/case names as duplicates. Offices may submit separate scans for one case, especially in workflows such as AOX. Review each submission separately and download/retain all applicable scans unless Support confirms otherwise.
Keywords: duplicate, same patient, same case, separate scan, AOX, 3Shape
Notes: This rule concerns portal files, not duplicate ABS case creation.

Question: Can source PDFs be deleted from the shared/intake folder?
Official Answer / SOP: No. Do not delete source PDFs during normal processing. Support advised that deleting source PDFs can cause the Rx to stop appearing or become inaccessible. If a file looks wrong or duplicated, escalate instead of deleting it.
Keywords: delete PDF, source file, Rx missing, folder, intake

Question: What should happen if Reject is clicked accidentally in 3Shape?
Official Answer / SOP: Do not intentionally reject normal cases. If Reject is clicked accidentally, document the situation in the case notes so the internal team has context. Continue the internal production process as directed and escalate the incident to the lead/support team.
Notes: Customer-facing follow-up is outside DE scope.

Question: What are Connections and Activity used for in 3Shape?
Official Answer / SOP: Connections may contain pending doctor connection/friend requests needed for future submissions. Activity can help verify office/address information for a doctor/Rx. Use these sections only when needed for case verification and follow the current team ownership rules.

Question: How are Aspen Dental accounts identified and matched?
Official Answer / SOP: When the doctor/Rx shows an Aspen-style identifier beginning with an A-number, search the patient in 3Shape and use the collaborator/drop-down information to retrieve the Aspen office number. In ABS, select the Aspen/OCASP office entry, not the Beacon option, because Beacon is a denture business unit.
Keywords: Aspen, A number, collaborator, OCASP, Beacon, office number
Notes: Use current account labels if ABS naming changes.
